html:
Arran was the medieval Arabic and Persian name for the lowland between the Kura and Araxes rivers in the eastern Caucasus, in what is now Azerbaijan. It was the heart of ancient Caucasian Albania. It is shown here in 1100.

Its old capital Barda was a great trading city in the 10th century, until Rus raiders sacked it in 943 or 944. Ganja then became the main city. From 951 the Kurdish Shaddadid dynasty ruled Arran from Ganja.

In 1075 the Seljuks took Ganja and Arran became part of their lands, later under the Eldiguzid atabegs. Ganja produced the great Persian poet Nizami Ganjavi, born there around 1141. To the north lay Shirvan, and in the hills to the west, Artsakh.
